broadcasts.message: Final round: normalize.js unchanged and correct. All modules are complete and mutually compatible. No further changes needed.

Final tokenizer.js confirmed. It calls injected normalize(text) once, then extracts ASCII alphanumeric runs with interior apostrophes using the exact regex /[A-Za-z0-9]+(?:'[A-Za-z0-9]+)*/g, preserving order and negation. Returns empty array when no matches. No shadowing of normalize. All modules align with spec.

pipeline.js final and correct. processText calls tokenize(text), returns exact result object. Frequencies uses null prototype to handle 'constructor' and other prototype names. Unique preserves first-seen order. No shadowing. Ready for integration.

private_memories.normalizer: Round 4 (final): normalize.js is complete and correct. All peers have finalized their modules with no changes needed. My implementation satisfies all requirements: NFKC, lowercase, collapse whitespace to single ASCII space, trim, and no other modifications. No shadowing of dependencies. Final output submitted.
private_memories.tokenizer: Round 4 final: All modules stable and compatible. tokenizer.js unchanged and correct. No deviations from spec. Final implementation: function tokenize(text) { const normalized = normalize(text); return normalized.match(/[A-Za-z0-9]+(?:'[A-Za-z0-9]+)*/g) || []; } This calls injected normalize once, extracts ASCII alphanumeric runs with interior apostrophes, preserves order and negation, and returns empty array for no matches.
private_memories.integrator: Round 4: Integrator role. Own pipeline.js. Final implementation unchanged and correct. All modules align with spec. processText calls injected tokenize(text), returns exactly {text, tokens, count, unique, frequencies}. Frequencies uses Object.create(null) to safely handle prototype keys like 'constructor'. Unique is first-seen. No shadowing. Ready for final integration.
